## Findings
- claim-1: Accepted dependency `162283c7d25bcc9b6cf77717e180ce1c85e4bdcbe2d0dbabc186aab75e18d126` (exit \(0\); script SHA-256 `16fd86d80765622e58e1da6f79707ddf13a2f664cccea1c42a38e798b9d07680`; output SHA-256 `818902094d31864cfaca06b0649fb4fc447ab0cc889c87f4d3a885dd54996e93`) computes the complete Pieri quotient for lower \((2,2,0,0,0,0,0,0)\), upper \((4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4)\), degrees \(4,\ldots,32\), and \(h\)-degrees \(1,2,3,4\): its quotient free ranks are \(1,1,2,1,1,0,\ldots,0\) in degrees \(4,5,6,7,8,9,\ldots,32\), respectively, and every torsion-invariant-factor list is empty. [artifact 162283c7d25bcc9b6cf77717e180ce1c85e4bdcbe2d0dbabc186aab75e18d126]
- claim-2: For \(Q=J_{2,6}/A_+J_{2,6}\), the dependency gives \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^{1+1+2+1+1}=\mathbb Z^6\): the five nonzero ranks total \(6\), all later degree quotients vanish, and empty Smith torsion lists give torsion-freeness.
- claim-3: The supplied source records that Theorem 5.4 supplies two generating sets, with \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\), and each has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [source-6@L14-L16|claim=ordinary-document] [source-6@L18-L42|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-4: In the case \(i=j=p=2,c=6\), one has \(a=\min(p,c)=2\), \(b=2\), and \(N=\binom42=6\). Using the accepted generation input, the two six-element families are \(\{s_{22},s_{32},s_{42},s_{33},s_{43},s_{44}\}\) and \(\{s_{22},s_{221},s_{222},s_{2211},s_{2221},s_{2222}\}\). Their images induce surjections \(\mathbb Z^6\twoheadrightarrow Q\cong\mathbb Z^6\). By the accepted indexed-family Nakayama criterion, each is a basis of \(Q\); hence no proper subfamily generates \(Q\), and therefore no proper subfamily generates \(J_{2,6}\). Thus both families are minimal for this case.
- claim-5: No new task-owned execution artifact was produced in this repair; the certificate instead relies on the exact accepted computation dependency named above.
## Strategy
Use accepted artifact `162283c7d25bcc9b6cf77717e180ce1c85e4bdcbe2d0dbabc186aab75e18d126` (exit \(0\); script SHA-256 `16fd86d80765622e58e1da6f79707ddf13a2f664cccea1c42a38e798b9d07680`; output SHA-256 `818902094d31864cfaca06b0649fb4fc447ab0cc889c87f4d3a885dd54996e93`). For \(Q=J_{2,6}/A_+J_{2,6}\), it gives ranks
\[
(1,1,2,1,1,0,\ldots,0)
\]
in degrees \(4,\ldots,32\), with empty torsion lists. Hence
\[
Q\cong\mathbb Z^{1+1+2+1+1}=\mathbb Z^6.
\]
For \(a=b=2\), the accepted two generating families each have
\(\binom42=6\) elements. Their images induce surjections \(\mathbb Z^6\twoheadrightarrow Q\cong\mathbb Z^6\); the accepted indexed-family Nakayama criterion makes these bases. Thus neither family has a proper generating subfamily, proving the \(i=j=p=2,c=6\) minimality corollary.
